name: ARMoR (Alliance for Reducing Microbial Resistance)
summary: Advocates for pull incentives, such as subscription payments, that fund the development of and access to new antimicrobials against drug-resistant infections.

lines.label: Advocacy for subscription-style pull incentives for new antibiotics (EU and member states)
lines.source: https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/srjXGXhsecmZvpEdq/two-years-of-doing-advocacy-on-antimicrobial-resistance (November 2025): $90,000 for 'our entire EU advocacy campaign for 2026' of a $280,000 budget. The rest (research on access to antibiotics in low- and middle-income countries, funded by Founders Pledge, GARDP/SECURE and a Gates regrant) has no model, so it doesn't count: the figure is per dollar of the advocacy the model covers.
